summary: guards/guards.ts registers 58 guards (not 60): 52 corpus-scope, 6 repo-scope; 6 gatesServing; forms 18 authored / 6 materialised / 34 none; 44 speak --json. Two further check-*.ts scripts exist on disk but are deliberately outside the registry (check-operation-contract.ts: 12 open findings; check-session-contract.ts: needs a session), recorded in tests/guard-registry.test.ts:142-152. No guard is imported by src/; the server's load-time refusal is the Zod loader, and check-routines.ts:74-76 states findings are 'guard findings rather than load failures'. Grouped by invariant, the 58 fall into 10 families. Only two families (schema/grammar validity: 4 guards; step-binding/variable dataflow on the YAML side: 9 guards) are substantially what a static type system over structured definitions would prove, and even those read technique signatures out of markdown headings and `{token}` reads out of prose. The rest read markdown structure, link targets, regex-matched phrasing, README tables, file layout, package-lock, site HTML, or human-authored ledgers. The ledger model (harmless/fix-later/live-bug) is documented in guards/README.md:49-67 and corpus ledgers/README.md; code implements it in check-binding-fidelity.ts:1277-1341 and variants in six other guards with differing verdict vocabularies. All 58 run in corpus CI as a merge gate (CORPUS .github/workflows/verify-corpus.yml:101-102); only the 6 gatesServing guards 'refuse' anything, and that is the experiment-sidecar reload preflight (tests/scripts/reload-exp-sidecar.sh:488; docs/http.md:68), not server start.

families.family: A1 Reference resolution over structured definitions
families.invariant: Every name a YAML/markdown definition uses to reach another artifact (technique ref, workflow id, directory name, launch target, map row, adapter kind, lens slug) resolves to exactly one thing the corpus holds.
families.type_checkable: partly — refs/workflow-identity/namespace-collision/launched-workflows are nominal lookups over parsed YAML and directory names (a module/namespace system could prove them); canonical-home-map reads a markdown table's home column (check-canonical-home-map.ts:17-18,60), harness-adapter-set parses numbered Protocol prose steps (check-harness-adapter-set.ts:16-21), prism-lens-reachability reads goal tables and frontmatter (check-prism-lens-reachability.ts:12-21).

families.family: A2 Markdown link and citation resolution
families.invariant: Every link or rule citation written in markdown lands on a file/heading/rule the reader will actually hold, in the form (bare vs anchored, name vs link) delivery semantics require.
families.type_checkable: no — all read markdown link syntax, GitHub heading slugs, fence state, `## Rules` headings and pre-section prose (check-resource-anchors.ts:4-13, check-citation-grain.ts:5-11, check-section-framing.ts:15-23, check-bootstrap-self-contained.ts:11-20); section-framing and unserved-operation-refs also consult human ledgers.

families.family: B1 Definition validity against schema and expression grammar
families.invariant: Every activity file and workflow.yaml validates against its Zod schema, every `when:` parses under the reference dialect, and a loop declares exactly the fields its loopType uses.
families.type_checkable: yes — these are schema validation and parsing over structured YAML (validate-activities.ts:34-60 calls safeValidateActivity; check-when-expression.ts:35-40 calls assertWhenAuthoring; check-loop-shape.ts:52-99 is a field-presence partition); a dependent type over the step kind would subsume loop-shape outright.

families.family: B2 Prose-stated contracts held against generated schemas and tool registrations
families.invariant: A construct named in canon prose, an inventory row, a described tool call, or a generated schema file agrees with the Zod source / tool registration that defines it.
families.type_checkable: partly — the target side is a JSON schema or registration a type system holds; the source side is inline code spans `tool_name { ... }` (check-tool-call-shape.ts:12-16), `**Fires on:**` lines (check-fires-on-ids.ts:5-16), backticked field paths in table rows (check-inventory-schema-agreement.ts:17-24), none of which a checker sees without a markdown parser. generated-schemas is a byte-equality check of rendered output (check-generated-schemas.ts:38).

families.family: C Step-to-technique binding and variable-bag dataflow
families.invariant: Every step binding resolves and conforms to the bound technique's signature; every read of the variable bag has a producer on every path; every produced value has a consumer; declared contracts (activity variables, routine signatures, workflow variable types/defaults/value sets) match what steps do; no step binds or composes a value from itself.
families.type_checkable: partly — the YAML half (step inputs/outputs maps, set targets, routine inputs/outputs/internals, workflow variables with type/defaultValue/values, loop variables) is a typed environment and a linear/affine effect system could prove read-after-write and consumed-once; but technique signatures are `###`/`####`/`#####` markdown headings plus a '(optional)' prose marker (check-binding-fidelity.ts:140-207), reads are regex `{token}` hits across markdown prose with fences blanked (609-637), dead-output treats a prose mention as a consumer (1048-1073), and activity-variables and binding-fidelity each carry a ledger of accepted exceptions.

families.family: D Checkpoint ordering, reachability and leakage
families.invariant: A gate is placed where its answer can still steer the run and shows only values already bound; a review-mode or stealth-mode run cannot auto-advance into or reach a mutating/disclosing step.
families.type_checkable: partly — ordinal-before-read (check-message-binding.ts:126-137), first-step kind (check-checkpoint-entry.ts:45-46) and exit reachability under a fixed bag (check-review-mode-gating.ts:15-17) are flow analyses over materialised steps a dependent/effect type could encode; but review-mode's ACCEPTED_HEADLESS_AUTO_ADVANCE is human judgement (52-62), stealth's layer (3) greps composed technique prose for `gh pr create` etc. (check-stealth-isolation.ts:16-19) and its layer (4) needs network.

families.family: E1 Technique file anatomy and I/O declaration form
families.invariant: A technique file follows the five-section template; every I/O id is a qualified snake_case noun; every declared value set is recorded by a protocol phase; every artifact output declares an audience, is JSON when agent-read, has a creation guide, and states status once.
families.type_checkable: partly — once the loader has parsed headings into a Technique record, template order/casing, audience enum and `.json` suffix are schema predicates (check-audience.ts:21-23 notes enum validity already lives in Zod); but protocol-shape counts `###` vs bare numbered lines (check-protocol-shape.ts:45-60), declared-values reads backticked tokens in Protocol prose (check-declared-values.ts:32-52), artifact-guides reads README tables and `## Template` headings (check-artifact-guides.ts:13-18), artifact-status-once reads fenced template blockquotes (check-artifact-status-once.ts:11-12).

families.family: E2 Single home / no duplicated declaration
families.invariant: A fact, rule text, checkpoint body, run of steps, nested output component, technique listing, or guard roster is authored in one place and referenced from others.
families.type_checkable: partly — duplicate-checkpoint, repeated-runs and activity-technique-overlap are structural equality over parsed YAML (check-repeated-runs.ts:14-25 signature reduction; check-activity-technique-overlap.ts:40-55) and decidable, though repeated-runs defers the verdict to a ledger; duplicate-rule, checkpoint-presentation and guard-roster regex-match prose (check-checkpoint-presentation.ts:16-26; check-guard-roster.ts:12-19); nested-output-home compares `####` headings across files with a triage.

families.invariant: Descriptions state WHAT not HOW; a conditional branch is a `>` note not an indented bullet; a routine signature describes the value not the reference site.
families.type_checkable: no — all three are regex phrase/shape sets over natural language (check-description-hygiene.ts:25-30 PROCEDURE_MARKERS; check-branch-as-step.ts:46-53 QUALIFIER; check-routine-signature-prose.ts:30-38 SITE_PROSE), self-described as 'a fail-closed *net*, not a full Detect walk' (check-description-hygiene.ts:9-11).

families.invariant: This repository's own sources, site, lockfile and instruction files are sound: links resolve, SVG text fits, no control bytes, no denylisted package versions, pinned corpus paths still exist, no duplicated agent instructions.
families.type_checkable: no — read HTML attributes, SVG geometry estimates (check-svg-layout.ts:3-14), raw bytes (check-source-encoding.ts:43-60), package-lock.json against scripts/known-bad-versions.json (check-lockfile-denylist.ts:23-25), string literals in TypeScript against corpus disk (check-pinned-corpus-paths.ts:41), and regex signatures in AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md. pinned-corpus-paths is registered scope corpus but reads this repo's TS.

binding_fidelity:
guards/check-binding-fidelity.ts (1375 lines; registry entry guards.ts:63-72, form authored, json true, gatesServing false).

READS. (a) Technique markdown signatures via fileSigDetailed (140-207): `## Inputs`/`## Outputs` → `### id` entries → `#### default` (input exempt from orphan), `#### artifact|audience|entry` reserved (118,124), any other `####` as a component, `#####` as entry fields; an input is optional when the first prose line matches OPTIONAL_INPUT_RE (201-204, shared with server via src/utils/binding-provenance.js at 69). (b) Registry per namespace via buildRegistry (219-263): root TECHNIQUE.md, group TECHNIQUE.md, ops; composed = own ∪ group ∪ root (241,246,256). (c) Step YAML via walkSteps (522-595) over parsed activities (801-813) and routines (678-704): technique bindings {name,inputs,outputs} (532-538), `kind: routine` with/outputs (545-552), set targets (553), validate targets and `when` as expression reads (557-562), setVariable/effect.setVariable/recordReply/variable (563-567), loop `over` plus item fields harvested by regex over JSON.stringify of the loop (572-592). (d) `{token}` reads via collectReads (621-637) over every technique .md, activity, routine and workflow.yaml with fenced blocks blanked but inline code kept (609-619); `variable:` lines in activities (628,632-635). (e) workflow.yaml variables/context and graph fan parameters/containers (356-386). (f) Resolution uses the server's parseTechniqueRef (274-303) with activity-group precedence (285-291). expressionReads (509-520) takes only the LEFT operand of each clause and skips ENV_PROBES gh/gpg/git/signing/workflows (497).

EMITS (Violation.check union at 956-958): binding-resolution (987) — step technique ref resolves to nothing, detail from TechniqueRefError (306-314); arg-conformance (1000,1003) — inputs/outputs key not in composed signature; orphan-input (1020-1023) — bound op's OWN non-default non-optional input with no producer in binding workflow, keyed per (workflow, op, input) seam, cleared if any site supplies it (975,1011,1026); read-resolution (1043) — `{token}` head not in scopeOf(wf) (875-893: declared ids, shared-namespace ids, producers, cross-workflow composed sigs) after PLACEHOLDER (320), file `{$local}`, container-member and fan-parameter exemptions; read-resolution for gate expressions (1057-1060); dead-output (1070-1073) — declared output with no consumer outside its file satisfying consumerReaches (934-947: same wf, shared lib, cross-workflow binder, dispatched child, borrow direction), exempt if `#### artifact`, interpolated in own artifact template (646-664), or lands in a read fan container (414-422); output-path-undeclared (1140-1144) — `{head.member}` where producer declares components but not that member; entry-field-undeclared (1204-1209) — `{item.field}` under a loop whose collection's component/own `entry` declares fields but not that one. Triage layer adds stale-triage (1316-1322) and misplaced-triage (1334-1338).

TRIAGE LEDGER. TRIAGE = ledgerPath(ROOT,'binding-fidelity-triage.json') (88; join(root,'ledgers',file) at workflows-root.ts:214-216). Types 1231-1243: verdict harmless|fix-later|live-bug, rationale key into file's rationales map, corpusSha. applyTriage (1277-1341): key = findingKey = check NUL site-minus-trailing-line NUL detail (guard-protocol.ts:53-58; 1245); no entry → reported with '[untriaged — classify it ...]' (1295-1298); live-bug → reported with rationale text (1302-1305); harmless/fix-later → suppressed, counted; entry matching nothing → stale-triage, naming a satisfier in another workflow if dead-output (1307-1322); entry whose cited line is not where the finding sits → misplaced-triage (1327-1338). triageStampNote (1256-1269) shells `git rev-parse`/`rev-list --count` to print distance from corpusSha, report-only. CLI (1343-1375): --emit-untriaged / --emit-all print JSON and exit 0, 'classification stays a human act' (1350); summary line (1363-1366); report() exits 1 on any remaining finding. CORPUS ledgers/binding-fidelity-triage.json at HEAD holds 58 harmless, 0 fix-later, 0 live-bug entries, corpusSha 7062aa0a (line 3), 11 rationales (4-16).

CLAIM vs DOES. Header (47-53) says 'no longer holds a stored baseline' and defers to check:delta, yet the file does load a ledger of accepted findings (1247-1250) — the distinction the code draws is that entries carry verdicts and cannot be regenerated. Header lists five checks (4-41) but the code emits seven kinds plus two triage kinds.
ledger_model:
DOCUMENTED: guards/README.md:49-59 — `harmless` 'correct by design — suppressed'; `fix-later` 'real debt — suppressed, but counted in the summary line'; `live-bug` 'reported, so the guard stays red until it is fixed'; 'A finding absent from the file is *untriaged* and reported; an entry matching nothing is *stale* and reported. There is no `--update-baseline`'. README:61-63 'A ledger is the exception ... not the shape a new guard starts from'; README:65-67 verdicts are judgements 'as they stood at `corpusSha`', printed distance does not fail. Corpus side: CORPUS ledgers/README.md:5-15 restates the three-verdict table and 'Each file is named for the check that reads it'.

IMPLEMENTED: binding-fidelity consults its ledger in applyTriage (check-binding-fidelity.ts:1277-1341) exactly as documented. Other guards follow the shape with DIFFERENT vocabularies: activity-variables reads ledgers/unproduced-read-triage.json for one family only, verdicts 'fix-later' | 'live-bug' (check-activity-variables.ts:106), suppresses only fix-later (149), emits duplicate-triage and stale-triage (136-158); repeated-runs reads ledgers/repeated-run-baseline.json with verdicts converging/unassigned/provisional (header 63-68; code 394-449, malformed verdict → repeated-run-baseline-verdict); unserved-operation-refs reads ledgers/unserved-operation-ref-triage.json, verdicts accepted/fix-later, BOTH suppress (header 43-49; code 164-193); section-framing, canonical-home-map, nested-output-home, artifact-guides read their own triage/baseline JSON (check-section-framing.ts:45-47; check-canonical-home-map.ts:49-53; check-nested-output-home.ts:54-58; check-artifact-guides.ts:234) with verdict typed as string; review-mode-gating keeps an in-code acceptance map ACCEPTED_HEADLESS_AUTO_ADVANCE and reports stale-acceptance (check-review-mode-gating.ts:52-62, 231-245). Every ledger-bearing guard reports a stale entry. CORPUS ledgers/ at HEAD holds 7 JSON files (binding-fidelity-triage, canonical-home-map-triage, nested-output-home-triage, repeated-run-baseline, section-framing-triage, unproduced-read-triage, unserved-operation-ref-triage); artifact-guide-baseline.json is absent, which check-artifact-guides.ts:26-27 says is the clean state.
refuse_vs_warn:
No guard runs at server load. grep of src/ for imports from guards/ returns nothing; check-routines.ts:74-76 records the decision: 'Findings are guard findings rather than load failures ... a routine contradicting its signature fails a guard run and a workflow carrying it still loads.' Load-time refusal is the Zod loader (check-audience.ts:21-23; check-technique-template.ts:19-22 says an unfilenameable artifact 'drops the technique with a logged warning').

WARN BEFORE MERGE (corpus CI): CORPUS .github/workflows/verify-corpus.yml:101-102 runs `npm run check:all` (package.json:78 → guards/check-all.ts) on every corpus pull request with WORKFLOWS_DIR=workflows (36); no --corpus-only, so all 58 registry guards including the 6 repo-scope ones run. Exit 2 (unmeasured) fails the job (99-100; check-all.ts:150). guards/README.md:25 'Corpus CI (`verify-corpus.yml`) runs the sweep; engine CI does not.' Engine CI (SERVER .github/workflows/verify.yml) runs only check:schemas (87) and check-tool-call-shape --root workflows (99), plus Vitest wrappers of guards that have tests (README.md:90-96).

REFUSE TO SERVE (sidecar preflight only): the 6 gatesServing guards — activities, loop-shape, refs, when-expression, workflow-identity, workflow-yaml — pinned by tests/guard-registry.test.ts:91-100. check-all.ts:11-15,100 exposes them as `--serving-only`; tests/scripts/reload-exp-sidecar.sh:488 runs `npx tsx guards/check-all.ts --root $CORPUS --serving-only` and refuses the container swap on failure (docs/http.md:68: 'A corpus that fails the guards refuses and leaves the container as it found it'; `--no-preflight` skips). Nothing in package.json start scripts (20-21) or the Dockerfile grep invokes a guard, so production `npm start` serves whatever the loader accepts.

Per-guard: check:binding etc. (package.json:11-19, 28-77) run singly, exit 0/1/2 via guard-protocol.ts:27-30. check:delta (check-delta.ts) compares findingKey sets for json guards (286-289) and exit code + new output lines otherwise (308-313).

open_questions: The task says 60 guards; guards.ts registers 58. The other two scripts on disk (check-operation-contract.ts, check-session-contract.ts) are deliberately unregistered (tests/guard-registry.test.ts:142-152). Should the lead count them? check-operation-contract is the one guard that crosses the activity-contract/technique-signature seam a type system would unify, and it is held out because it is red.

Does any production start path (npm start, Dockerfile, docker-publish.yml) run the serving preflight? grep of package.json:20-21, scripts/, Dockerfile* found no guard invocation; only tests/scripts/reload-exp-sidecar.sh:488 does. Not verified by reading the Dockerfile in full.

Three guards police overlapping read/producer invariants over the variable bag with different scoping rules: binding-fidelity read-resolution (per-workflow scope incl. shared libraries), activity-variables (per activity graph incl. included activities), routines (per routine signature). A single typed environment would replace all three; whether their exemption lists (PLACEHOLDER, AMBIENT_CONTEXT_IDS, ENV_PROBES, fan containers, ledgers) are expressible as types is the lead's question.
The binding-fidelity ledger's corpusSha (7062aa0a) differs from the corpus HEAD under test (15860ff); triageStampNote prints the distance only when run. I did not run the guards.
guards/README.md:92-96 says the set of guards that are also Vitest tests should be read from tests/ by grep; I did not enumerate them.

Whether a Bend proof could consume technique signatures at all depends on the markdown→Technique parse the loader performs (src/loaders/markdown-technique-loader.js); several guards (audience, declared-values, artifact-guides) route through tryLoadMarkdownTechnique while binding-fidelity re-parses headings itself (140-207) — two parsers of one format.
